nodes.content: Build an incremental dependency analyzer that prevents stale artifacts despite generated inputs, conditional dependencies, and concurrent filesystem changes.
requirements: Match clean-build outputs across 1,000 adversarial edit sequences, including dependency creation and deletion.
Rebuild at most 10% more actions than an exact dependency oracle across those sequences.

nodes.content: Use producer-aware graphs, traced conditional reads and absence probes, versioned snapshots, and commit-time validation before atomically publishing artifacts.
How can snapshot validation detect concurrent creation of a previously absent generated input without invalidating unrelated actions?
Commit-time revalidation of per-path absence probes and producer epochs catches concurrent generated-input creation with under 10% excess rebuilds.
Implement per-path absence probes and producer epochs; race generated-file creation with commits, measuring mismatches and unrelated rebuilds over 1,000 sequences.
Implement EpochProbe’s absence checks and producer epochs; test 1,000 concurrent generated-file races against clean-build hashes and oracle rebuild counts.
EpochProbe matched all 1,000 clean-build hashes, missed no generated-file creations, and rebuilt 4,182 actions versus the oracle’s 4,050 (3.3% excess).
Stress EpochProbe commit-time absence validation with concurrent creations and 200 unrelated path edits; compare stale hashes and excess rebuilds.
In 200 additional unrelated-edit races, EpochProbe rebuilt 253 actions versus 220 oracle actions (15% excess), despite zero stale hashes.
Can producer-epoch validation be scoped to traced paths to eliminate unrelated-edit rebuilds without missing generated-file creation?
Path-scoped producer epochs for traced reads and absence probes preserve zero stale hashes while reducing unrelated-edit excess below 10%.
Replace global producer epochs with traced-path epochs; rerun generated-file races and unrelated edits against clean-build hashes and oracle counts.
Implement PathEpoch’s traced-path producer versions and rerun 1,000 adversarial sequences plus 200 unrelated-edit races against clean builds and oracle.
PathEpoch produced one stale hash across 1,000 sequences when a condition activated an untraced generated include; excess fell to 2%.
Revalidate conditional guards and scoped include-search directory epochs alongside traced paths to catch newly activated includes with under 10% excess.
Add conditional-guard fingerprints and include-search directory epochs to PathEpoch, then replay activation races and compare hashes and oracle rebuilds.
Implement GuardEpoch, then replay 1,000 sequences and 200 unrelated-edit races against PathEpoch, clean-build hashes, and oracle rebuild counts.
Across 200 unrelated-edit races, PathEpoch had zero stale hashes and 2% excess; GuardEpoch reached 12% excess over 1,000 sequences.
Reject PathEpoch’s unguarded validation and GuardEpoch’s broad directory epochs; retain guard checks while narrowing directory watches to active search scopes.
Use guard-aware dependency certificates with ordered include-search probes and producer versions, revalidating affected predicates before atomic publication.
How can ordered include-search probes detect a newly generated earlier-priority header without invalidating actions on unrelated directory edits?
Commit-time validation of guarded, higher-priority filename absence probes catches generated-header shadowing without invalidating unrelated directory edits.
Implement guarded, ordered filename-absence probes; race generated header shadowing and unrelated directory edits, comparing clean-build hashes and oracle rebuilds.
Across 300 shadowing and 200 unrelated-edit races, guarded probes produced zero stale hashes and 2.5% excess rebuilds.
GuardedProbe module stores guard fingerprints and ordered filename-absence probes, with commit-time checks for generated-header shadowing.
Schedule generated-input producers to a dynamic graph fixed point, invalidating consumers when producers or outputs disappear.
When a generator is removed, how should its vanished outputs invalidate consumers that previously resolved those paths?
Tombstoning removed producer outputs and incrementing their path versions will reschedule former consumers before they reuse stale artifacts.
Track producer-output tombstones and path versions; replay generator removals, fallback resolutions, and concurrent deletes against clean builds and oracle rebuilds.
Extend GuardedProbe with output tombstones and path-version invalidation; replay generator removals and fallback headers against clean builds and oracle.
In 250 generator-removal and fallback cases, tombstones yielded zero stale hashes and 3.1% excess rebuilds versus the oracle.
Use optimistic filesystem snapshots with journal-backed revalidation and atomic publication to reject mixed-version traces under concurrent edits.
How can journal-backed validation catch read-to-publish filesystem races while retrying only actions whose observed paths changed?
An edit-serialized journal barrier around validation and publication, with certificate-scoped retries, yields zero stale hashes and under 10% excess rebuilds.
Implement journal-barrier validation and certificate-scoped retries; inject read-to-publish edits across 1,000 sequences, comparing clean-build hashes and oracle rebuilds.
Across 1,000 sequences, one out-of-band rename bypassed the journal barrier, producing a stale hash; excess rebuilds were 4%.
Use immutable filesystem snapshots and kernel change notifications, reconciling out-of-band renames against dependency certificates before atomic publication.
How can publication detect an out-of-band rename affecting a certified path without invalidating actions for unrelated filesystem events?
Add kernel rename-event reconciliation and pre-publication certificate checks; stress watched-path renames versus unrelated events, tracking hash mismatches and excess rebuilds.
Extend GuardedProbe with immutable snapshots and kernel rename reconciliation; race watched-path and unrelated renames, comparing hashes and oracle rebuilds.
Across 400 rename races, snapshot-and-notification reconciliation caught every watched-path rename: zero stale hashes and 4.8% excess rebuilds.
Force notification-queue overflow during out-of-band renames; recheck GuardedProbe certificates against immutable snapshots, measuring stale hashes and oracle rebuilds.
In 120 notification-overflow rename races, one lost watched-path event produced a stale artifact despite immutable build snapshots.
How can snapshot reconciliation detect watched-path renames after notification overflow without rescanning and rebuilding unrelated actions?
After overflow, reconcile certificate path identities, digests, and absence probes against a fresh snapshot; retry only changed actions.
Implement overflow-triggered certificate reconciliation across snapshot generations; replay rename bursts and unrelated edits against clean builds and oracle counts.
Use n41’s rename baseline and n43’s overflow failure as regression fixtures to implement GuardedProbe’s snapshot certificate checks and scoped retries.
Across 120 overflow races, certificate reconciliation yielded zero stale hashes and rebuilt 286 actions versus 278 oracle actions (2.9% excess).
Extend GuardedProbe using n48’s overflow fixture; race watched and unrelated renames during reconciliation and publication, comparing hashes and oracle rebuilds.
In 300 publication-race cases, one watched rename after reconciliation caused a stale hash; unrelated-event excess stayed at 3%.
What publication protocol prevents a watched rename between certificate reconciliation and artifact commit without retrying unrelated actions?
A kernel-enforced workspace mutation barrier spanning final reconciliation and atomic publication prevents rename races while retaining certificate-scoped retries.
Prototype a mutation-frozen workspace snapshot for final certificate checks and publication; benchmark watched renames, unrelated edits, and oracle rebuild counts.
Extend GuardedProbe’s n48 overflow reconciliation with a kernel-enforced mutation barrier; replay n50 publication races against clean-build hashes and oracle.
Across 300 publication races, the mutation barrier eliminated stale hashes (1 to 0) with 3.4% excess rebuilds versus oracle.
Adopt certificate-scoped overflow reconciliation and mutation-barrier publication: overflow tests passed, unguarded publication failed, and guarded publication eliminated stale hashes.
